evidence.claim: Granite spires and a stage-road canyon link Albion with Oakley.
evidence.quote: The City of Rocks Backcountry Byway weaves through the Albion Mountain Range and rural landscapes peppered with towering granite spires.

evidence.claim: a stage-road canyon
evidence.quote: Much of the road is through a narrow canyon with high volcanic cliffs. This was the route of the historic Kelton-Boise Stage Line.

evidence.claim: link Albion with Oakley
evidence.quote: Begin at Albion and proceed south to Connor Creek Junction along Idaho 77. Continuing south through Elba and Almo, arrive at the City of Rocks National Reserve. From the Reserve, the byway heads north and follows Birch Creek to the City of Oakley where it joins Idaho 27.

evidence.claim: The City of Rocks Backcountry Byway crosses the Albion Mountains through rural country punctuated by granite spires.
evidence.quote: The City of Rocks Backcountry Byway weaves through the Albion Mountain Range and rural landscapes peppered with towering granite spires.

evidence.claim: Its paved approach becomes a narrow, winding road between Connor Creek and Almo, then gravel from Almo to Oakley.
evidence.quote: Connor Creek to Almo is a narrow winding paved road, and from Almo to Oakley the road is graveled until it joins Idaho 27 at Oakley.

evidence.claim: Visit Idaho includes this backcountry route among the state’s scenic byways and emphasizes its geology and rural landscape.
evidence.quote: 31 Byways. 31 Ways to Be Inspired.

evidence.claim: The tourism office gives the 49.4-mile drive a travel time of one hour and 18 minutes.
evidence.quote: Length 49.4 miles 79.5 km Time 1 hour, 18 minutes

evidence.claim: Along Birch Creek, the landscape closes into a narrow canyon with high volcanic cliffs, between Middle Mountain on the west and the Albion range on the east.
evidence.quote: The most enclosed landscape on the byway is along Birch Creek between Middle Mountain to the west and the Albion Mountain Range to the east. Much of the road is through a narrow canyon with high volcanic cliffs.

evidence.claim: In the 1840s and 1850s, California Trail wagon trains left the Raft River valley and crossed City of Rocks on their way over Granite Pass into Nevada.
evidence.quote: During the 1840s and 1850s, wagon trains on the California Trail left the Raft River valley and traveled through the area and over Granite Pass into Nevada.

evidence.claim: After the transcontinental railroad was completed in 1869, regional wagon and stage routes continued serving places beyond the rails.
evidence.quote: With the completion of the first transcontinental railroad on 9 May 1869, the overland wagon routes began to pass into history. However, wagons and stage lines saw continued use on regional supply routes that spread out from the railroad line to cities not on the railway line(s).

evidence.claim: The Kelton-to-Boise stage route passed through City of Rocks; the modern byway follows its corridor along Birch Creek.
evidence.quote: Much of the road is through a narrow canyon with high volcanic cliffs. This was the route of the historic Kelton-Boise Stage Line.

evidence.claim: The Kelton-to-Boise stage route passed through City of Rocks
evidence.quote: The Kelton stage route passed through the City of Rocks

evidence.claim: Begin in Albion on Idaho 77, continue to Connor Creek Junction, then travel through Elba and Almo to City of Rocks National Reserve.
evidence.quote: Begin at Albion and proceed south to Connor Creek Junction along Idaho 77. Continuing south through Elba and Almo, arrive at the City of Rocks National Reserve.

evidence.claim: Beyond the reserve, the route turns north along Birch Creek toward Oakley and its junction with Idaho 27.
evidence.quote: From the Reserve, the byway heads north and follows Birch Creek to the City of Oakley where it joins Idaho 27.

evidence.claim: Almo is a ranching community below 10,399-foot Cache Peak, just over two miles east of City of Rocks National Reserve.
evidence.quote: It is a ranching community situated in the shadow of 10,399 foot Cache Peak.

evidence.claim: just over two miles east of City of Rocks National Reserve
evidence.quote: Almo is just over 2 miles (3.2 km) east away from the City of Rocks National Reserve

evidence.claim: The town developed around a post office established in 1881 on land that had been part of Myron B. Durfee’s ranch.
evidence.quote: Almo was established around a post office in 1881. It had previously been part of a ranch belonging to Myron B. Durfee

evidence.claim: By the turn of the century, Almo had a school, a brass band and a theatrical group as well as a store and post office.
evidence.quote: Almo at the turn of the century boasted a store, a post office, a school, a brass band, a theatrical group

evidence.claim: The reserve’s headquarters is in Almo.
evidence.quote: The Reserve headquarters is located in the gateway community of Almo.

evidence.claim: The visitor center for both the reserve and Castle Rocks State Park is at the south end of town, linking this ranching settlement with the two protected landscapes.
evidence.quote: The visitor center for the National Reserve and Castle Rocks State Park is located at the south end of town.

evidence.claim: Axle grease became a writing material at City of Rocks.
evidence.quote: Names or initials of emigrants written in axle grease are still visible on Register Rock

evidence.claim: California-bound emigrants left names and initials on Register Rock, where those marks remain visible alongside a landscape bearing wagon-wheel ruts.
evidence.quote: Names or initials of emigrants written in axle grease are still visible on Register Rock, and ruts from wagon wheels can be seen in some of the rocks.

evidence.claim: During the 1840s and 1850s, wagon trains crossed this granite country from the Raft River valley toward Granite Pass and Nevada.
evidence.quote: During the 1840s and 1850s, wagon trains on the California Trail left the Raft River valley and traveled through the area and over Granite Pass into Nevada.

evidence.claim: The area became a national reserve in 1988 for its historical and geological values, scenery and recreation.
evidence.quote: The area's historical and geological values, scenery, and opportunities for recreation led to its designation as City of Rocks National Reserve in 1988.

evidence.claim: The granite rises from rolling sagebrush country. Erosion along fractures has shed thin plates and scales from the rocks, shaping the formations that frame the emigrant route.
evidence.quote: Rock formations in the reserve developed through an erosion process called exfoliation, during which thin rock plates and scales sloughed off along joints in the rocks.

evidence.claim: The granite rises from rolling sagebrush country.
evidence.quote: City of Rocks is an encirclement of granite rising out of the rolling sagebrush country in south-central Idaho.

evidence.claim: Names and initials written in axle grease remain visible on Register Rock.
evidence.quote: Names or initials of emigrants written in axle grease are still visible on Register Rock

evidence.claim: Oakley’s historic district includes Victorian houses and the Howells Opera House.
evidence.quote: Oakley's National Historic District includes many Victorian homes, and the turn-of-the-century Howells Opera House.

evidence.claim: The theater, completed in 1907, was built from local quartzite known as Oakley stone.
evidence.quote: The building was constructed using a local variety of quartzite referred to as Oakley stone.

evidence.claim: completed in 1907
evidence.quote: The building construction began in 1904 and was completed in 1907

evidence.claim: Its square gable false front has a central doorway flanked by segmental-arched openings.
evidence.quote: The opera house has a square gable false front with a central door flanked by segmental-arched openings.

evidence.claim: Nearby quarries produce Oakley Stone for use as a building material. Within the town’s historic district, stone and brick buildings stand alongside its Victorian houses.
evidence.quote: Nearby quarries produce the distinctive Oakley Stone which is a popular home constuction material

evidence.claim: Within the town’s historic district, stone and brick buildings stand alongside its Victorian houses.
evidence.quote: The entire town is listed due to the number of stone and brick buildings that are over a century old.

evidence.claim: When demolition was discussed in the 1970s, local performers formed the Oakley Valley Arts Council and bought the building.
evidence.quote: During the 1970s, when the opera house had fallen into a state of disrepair and demolition of the house was being discussed, the performing arts community within Oakley formed the Oakley Valley Arts Council and purchased the house.

evidence.claim: The council continues to stage seasonal performances there.
evidence.quote: Today the Oakley Valley Arts Council continues to put on seasonal performances here.
